title: Ripples reflect a spectrum of synchronous spiking activity in human anterior temporal lobe (Tong et al., 2021): figure-level iEEG, micro-LFP and spiking arrays (derivative)
description: A derivative repackaging of the authors' public Dryad release accompanying Tong et al. (2021), containing figure-level arrays for panels of Figures 1-4. It includes epoched and band-filtered iEEG, micro-LFP from 96-channel Utah arrays, time-frequency power, ripple rasters and spike indices from the human anterior temporal lobe, recorded during a paired-associates verbal memory task in patients with drug-resistant epilepsy. The data support analyses showing that ripples reflect a spectrum of synchronous spiking activity. Raw continuous recordings are not included.
methods_description: Participants with drug-resistant epilepsy were implanted with subdural and depth contacts, and six also had 96-channel microelectrode arrays in the anterior temporal lobe, at the NIH Clinical Center during a paired-associates verbal episodic memory task. iEEG was sampled at 1000 Hz, with line-noise removal and Morlet wavelet power. Micro-LFP was low-pass filtered at 500 Hz and downsampled to 1000 Hz, and single units were manually spike sorted. Ripples were detected in the 80-120 Hz band using a Hilbert envelope threshold of 2 SD for at least 25 ms with a peak above 3 SD.
